metadata.note: The Barre & Montpelier Street Railway, the electric trolley line between Vermont's capital and its granite city - the third Montpelier-area passenger operation in this dataset, alongside the steam Montpelier & Wells River in montpelier_wells_river_railroad.geojson and the Vermont Central branch in vermont_central_railroad.geojson. Note the name: the modern 'Montpelier & Barre Railway' is a diesel granite short line reorganized in 2013 and is a different thing entirely; the historic electric operation ran under the Barre & Montpelier name. It is also a street railway rather than a true interurban - american-rails.com counts only the Springfield Terminal as a genuine Vermont interurban, the rest being local streetcar services - so it is tagged mode streetcar here. GEOMETRY IS THE WEAKEST IN THIS DATASET AND SHOULD BE TREATED AS SCHEMATIC: the tracks are long gone and OpenStreetMap holds no trace of them, so the line is drawn as a modern road route (OSRM) through the streets the sources name - State Street, Main Street and Barre Street in Montpelier, then the Barre-Montpelier Road corridor southeast through Berlin into Barre. That corridor is right, but the drawn alignment is today's pavement, not a surveyed trolley route, and modern road realignments are not corrected for. Era boundaries follow sourced corporate milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not real timetables.
sources: https://www.american-rails.com/vrmtinterstreetcar.html (the Barre & Montpelier Street Railway began operations in June 1889 connecting downtown Montpelier with Barre; in Montpelier the trolleys ran from Bailey Avenue, down State Street to Main Street to Barre Street and onto Pioneer Street; renamed the Barre & Montpelier Traction & Power Company in 1919 and in operation until the late 1920s, when rail service was replaced by buses; the fleet ran 12 two-man motor passenger cars and 2 one-man cars; Vermont had only one true interurban, the Springfield Terminal, the rest being local streetcar services)
https://www.chicagorailfan.com/aatvt1.html (Barre/Montpelier transit chronology: Barre & Montpelier Traction Co. 1898-1925, Vergennes Power Co. 1925-1927, streetcars discontinued 1927)

https://vermonthistory.org/age-of-trolleys-1901 (Vermont Historical Society: Vermont's first street railroad was the Winooski and Burlington Horse Railroad in 1885, electrified by 1887; at their height the state's trolleys carried 10 million passengers a year; traction companies developed parks at the ends of their lines, including Benjamin's Falls Park between Montpelier and Barre, near the little stream that runs by the State Garage)
OSRM public routing service over OpenStreetMap road data (drawn corridor, ODbL)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Frequency for every era is estimated, as is the 25 km/h running speed. The sources conflict on corporate history: american-rails dates the rename to Barre & Montpelier Traction & Power to 1919, while the chicagorailfan chronology lists a Barre & Montpelier Traction Co. from 1898 to 1925 and a Vergennes Power Co. from 1925 to 1927 - the era boundaries here use 1889, 1919, 1925 and 1927 and do not resolve the disagreement. The date of electrification is not stated by any source found; an 1889 start may well have been horse or steam power initially. The exact Montpelier terminus at Bailey Avenue and the Pioneer Street end of the city trackage are not reflected in the drawn geometry, which runs State Street to Main Street to Barre Street only.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.

segments.note: The Barre & Montpelier Street Railway began running in June 1889, tying the capital to the granite city eight miles away. In Montpelier the cars ran from Bailey Avenue down State Street to Main Street to Barre Street and out onto Pioneer Street, then followed the Barre-Montpelier road southeast. Like most traction companies it built its own destinations at the ends of the line - Benjamin's Falls Park lay between the two cities, near the little stream by the State Garage. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Renamed the Barre & Montpelier Traction & Power Company in 1919 - the standard arrangement of the era, where the trolleys and the electricity that ran them belonged to the same company. The fleet was a dozen two-man passenger motors plus two set up for one-man operation. Vermont's trolleys together carried something like 10 million passengers a year at their height. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The end came quickly. The chicagorailfan chronology shows the property under a Vergennes Power Co. from 1925, and in 1927 the Yellow Bus Company - already running Barre to Montpelier to Burlington - was allowed to pick up local riders. The streetcars were discontinued that year, and Montpelier and Barre have been connected by buses ever since. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
